what: campaign_v7 recorded 0 promotions across cycles 30-68 while its active model stayed frozen at cycle 29. This measures whether that reflects a trainer that stopped learning or a gate that cannot see the size of gain the trainer produces. It is the second: the checkpoint lineage accumulated +25.4 Elo that the gate rejected every time.
engine: PieBot at box commit 568163a (identical to local 3fd664a for all training and engine paths)

protocol.mode: --same-search (both arms use the baseline searcher; model-only A/B)
protocol.note: Both arms run at EvalBlend 50, the live active_model_blend_percent, so no blend confound.

D1_cycle68_vs_cycle29.interpretation: The cycle-68 training checkpoint is decisively stronger than the frozen cycle-29 active model. The lower confidence bound is well clear of zero.

D0_absolute_pst_reference.interpretation: Reads flat, but at 200 games per arm this comparison cannot resolve a difference below roughly 45 Elo. It is uninformative at the effect size in question and is NOT evidence against D1.

corroboration_from_the_campaign_itself.note: Two independently powered measurements taken seven cycles apart agree on steady accumulation of roughly +0.5 to +0.65 Elo per cycle against the frozen baseline. Every gate screen in the retained window was positive (+14.5, +29.0, +29.0, +14.5, +29.0 Elo) and every cycle was still rejected.

root_cause.llr_formula: autopilot._gsprt_decision: llr = pairs * delta1 * (mean - delta1/2) / variance
root_cause.truncation_rule: autopilot._run_model_gate converts an inconclusive SPRT into decision=reject (reason max-pairs-inconclusive)
root_cause.why_it_rejected: A true effect of +25.4 Elo (mean pair delta 0.146) sits barely above the +21.8 Elo indifference point, so the log-likelihood ratio has almost no drift and the test wanders until it is truncated -- and truncation is recorded as a rejection. Rejection was the default outcome for exactly the size of gain this trainer produces.
root_cause.conventional_bounds_for_this_tier: [0, 10] Elo at alpha=beta=0.05 (chessprogramming.org SPRT table). At the shipped bounds a genuinely +10 Elo candidate passes about 17% of the time; at [0, 10] it passes about 95%.

sizing.basis: pairs = 2*variance*ln((1-beta)/alpha)/delta1^2 at the design point; variance 0.8504 measured over 500 pairs above
sizing.why_the_screen_threshold_rose: With a tight delta1 a null candidate needs as many pairs to reject as a real one needs to accept, so every cycle would pay the full confirmation. A positive screen threshold keeps that cost off cycles with nothing to promote; at 48 screen pairs it escalates about 35% of null cycles and about 77% of genuine +25 Elo cycles.

replay_validation.what: The recorded pair outcomes of cycle 61's rejected confirmation were replayed through a faithful reimplementation of autopilot._gsprt_decision under both the shipped and the proposed parameters. This tests the change against real game data rather than against an assumed effect size.
replay_validation.source: cycles/cycle_000061/gate_compare_confirmation.json, 240 pairs reconstructed from game_results by pair_index

shipped_delta1_0.25_max_pairs_300.note: hit the reject BOUND -- the old gate did not merely fail to confirm this candidate, it actively concluded against it

proposed_delta1_0.0575_max_pairs_1600.note: positive and climbing toward the +2.944 accept bound; the replay ran out of played pairs because the shipped run stopped at 240

replay_validation.conclusion: Under the proposed parameters cycle 61 would have been promoted at roughly 423 pairs. The sign of the log-likelihood ratio flips from -3.86 to +1.67 on identical data, which isolates the parameters as the cause of the rejection.

max_pairs_sizing_check.note: Both observed variances conclude within the cap. A cap below ~1520 would silently reconvert the tighter H1 into an unconditional reject at the higher observed variance.

caveats: The Elo figures are self-play logistic Elo at 150 ms, not anchor Elo. They measure this net against this net, not against Stockfish.
No arch-v2 net has ever been measured against the pinned SF16 anchor. Every ladder number in this campaign (1892 / 2146 / 2422, and S6's +83) used the v1 h64 net at blend 25.
The +0.65 Elo/cycle rate is an average over 39 cycles against a frozen baseline. It is not guaranteed to continue, and it should be re-measured after the first promotion moves the baseline.
